title: Diwali at Times Square Returns October 24 for Its 11th Edition
excerpt: Sammaan For All's free festival takes over Broadway on October 24, 2026, with a bazaar, a Kids Zone, a diya-lighting countdown and a concert headlined by Kanika Kapoor and Raja Kumari.
body:
• Diwali at Times Square returns on Saturday, October 24, 2026, for its 11th edition, presented by P&G and Tide and Toyota and organised by Sammaan For All.
  • The free festival takes over Broadway between 46th and 48th Streets in Manhattan, with a Diwali Bazaar, a Kids Zone, cultural performances and an evening concert.
  • Kanika Kapoor, Raja Kumari, Rishi Singh and Shanmukha Priya headline the Light Up Times Square Concert, after a Diya Lighting Ceremony with a countdown on the Ball Drop Tower.
  • Reader utility: entry is free with no ticket required on October 24; an Awards and Gala Dinner honouring Indian American achievers takes place the evening before, October 23, at Tribeca 360.

Diwali at Times Square will return to Manhattan on Saturday, October 24, 2026, for its 11th edition, organiser Sammaan For All announced on October 19. The festival, presented by P&G and Tide and Toyota, brings the Hindu festival of lights to Broadway between 46th and 48th Streets, in what organisers call the Center of the Universe.

The programme was unveiled at a press conference hosted by the Consulate General of India in New York on October 14, where Deputy Consul General Vishal Harsh extended his support to the celebrations. Founder and president Neeta Bhasin announced the performer lineup and the two-day schedule, according to the announcement carried by PR Newswire.

A full day at the Crossroads of the World

The October 24 festival opens with a Diwali Bazaar and a dedicated Kids Zone, where children can paint diyas, create rangoli art and take Bollywood dance lessons. Vendors will offer product sampling, and partners will run educational stalls through the day.

The afternoon belongs to the 'Colors of India and America' programme, with performances by Indian, Indo-Caribbean and Hispanic dance groups. In the evening, dignitaries will gather for the Diya Lighting Ceremony, with a countdown displayed on the Ball Drop Tower screen, leading into the Light Up Times Square Concert. Full event details are on the official Diwali at Times Square website.

"Diwali celebrates the triumph of light over darkness, knowledge over ignorance, and hope over despair. I commend Samman For All-Diwali At Times Square for bringing communities together in one of the world's most iconic public spaces to share the joy of this festival."

— Binaya S. Pradhan, Consul General of India in New York

Kanika Kapoor and Raja Kumari headline the concert

The concert lineup for the 11th edition mixes Bollywood playback, Indian American hip-hop and reality-show winners. Kanika Kapoor, the Filmfare Award-winning singer, is joined by Grammy-nominated Indian American rapper Raja Kumari, Indian Idol 13 winner Rishi Singh and Indian Idol 12 finalist Shanmukha Priya.

The bill also includes singer-rapper Sparsh Shah, known as "Purhythm," and New York's 'Singing Chef' Kunal Lamba. Colors TV will broadcast the celebration.

A gala the night before

The festival weekend starts on Friday, October 23, with an Awards and Gala Dinner at Tribeca 360. The dinner honours Indian American contributions in philanthropy, innovation, medicine and entrepreneurship, according to the organisers.

Sponsors include platinum sponsor Gopi, gold sponsor Xoom by PayPal, and the State Bank of India. Bhasin also acknowledged New York City's Office of Community Engagement for its continued support.

Why it matters for the diaspora

Since its first edition, the festival has put Diwali on one of the most photographed stages in the world, two weeks ahead of Diwali itself, on Sunday, November 8, 2026. For families in the New York tri-state area, the free, no-ticket format makes it the easiest large Diwali outing of the season: arrive in Midtown, and the bazaar, kids' activities and concert are all in the open plaza. Readers on the West Coast can compare it with the Bay Area season that opened this month — see our coverage of Cupertino's Diwali celebration at Memorial Park.

"As we begin a new decade of Diwali at Times Square, we carry forward the light that our community and our partners have shared with us over the years," Bhasin said. "It is so important to instill in South Asian American youth a sense of pride in their heritage, and to show the world the values of art, culture and togetherness that Diwali stands for."

What to know before you go

The festival runs Saturday, October 24, on Broadway between 46th and 48th Streets, and admission is free. Families with young children will get the most from the afternoon Bazaar and Kids Zone, while the Diya Lighting Ceremony and concert are the evening draw. Organisers have not published a full hour-by-hour timetable, so check the official site closer to the date before fixing travel plans.
